title: Native Windows lab provisioning
summary: The native Windows lab adapter uses Windows OpenSSH and PowerShell, an interactive scheduled task for desktop screenshots and console checks, and profile goldens that preserve live identities. Standard-user task control uses native Task Scheduler COM. Desktop provisioning validates the stored password against the local account before writing autologon, retains the LSA password and removes AutoLogonCount so an old logon counter cannot disable autologon. After a cold start, power-on waits for Explorer in the lab user's console session. Provisioning grants inheritable access at the golden root before creating fresh golden directories, so a rerun does not explicitly walk sealed golden contents. SSH is key-only from any address. Human RDP is allowed over verified Tailscale self addresses or adapters, never the public internet; an SSH forward remains available for bootstrap. A private bounded SYSTEM probe verifies tailnet identity without selecting an administrator's Tailscale profile. Fresh setup teaches localhost SSH/RDP password custody and Start > Tailscale > Get Started with the existing account and expected-device approval. Provisioning privately backs up and disables only the verified vendor tray shortcut, refusing unexpected or renamed startup entries. SYSTEM probe receipts retain exact allowlisted failures and replace unknown errors with a fixed safe reason. Acceptance requires two separate cold boots with completed automatic standard-user logon, unchanged tailnet identity and startup key, private routes, and no tray autostart or intervening profile repair; command success alone does not prove persistence. Harness desktop and CLI sign-ins require separate visible-app and real-request proof before goldens. Provisioning and live restoration require separate machine receipts before readiness is claimed. Agents drive any lab desktop app with yoke qa mission desktop, launch apps with host-command --gui-session and look with yoke test-machine screenshot, all in the auto-logged-on console session, so the controller needs no RDP client or Windows App; an RDP client is optional for a person watching or the one-time bootstrap sign-in, whose private RDP password prompt is an operator handoff. Keep the lab on until active setup, sign-ins and QA finish, without countdowns or idle deallocation; verify and report final deallocation. Administrator staging cleanup failures remain fatal with named recovery and retain completed command diagnostics privately; they do not prove the primary command failed. Native vendor PowerShell installers decode raw UTF-8 response bytes consistently for binary and text media types. The guide names built-in Windows PowerShell 5.1 by its full executable path. Claude native installation completes its User PATH immediately, preserving existing entries and registry value kind; fresh logon discovery needs separate proof. Live per-user Windows packaged-app containers and Claude desktop data remain on the host through capture and reset; their app settings are not golden-restored. Claude CLI settings are captured and restored. Golden PATH snapshots retain raw values, registry kinds and absence; reset validates them before any mirror and verifies them after restoration. Older goldens without raw metadata require recapture. Console screen reads use the same interactive session as launch and input, opening CONOUT$ rather than redirected standard output; failures retain numeric Win32 and session context. Input resolves the uniquely titled visible host and validates user, session and foreground before sending keys, retaining the client PID for buffer reads and cleanup. Screenshot tasks request hidden windows so capture machinery does not obscure the application under review. Private robocopy logs retain copy failure diagnostics, which remain fatal. Canonical goldens also require the operator to review Claude Code’s one-time bypass warning personally; sign-in is separate and directly writing the acknowledgement is not proof. Reset removes profile links the golden lacks, keeping Windows' System-marked profile junctions, and refuses windows_reset_uv_state_left when uv-managed Python the golden lacks survives; failed console installs keep the last 40 lines of both output streams. Reset removes YokeQaMission scratch the running execution does not own. Goldens hold no command stage folders or uv Python registry: the mirror skips root .yoke-stage-* folders, capture refuses windows_profile_not_pristine while a stage folder or HKCU\Software\Python\Astral is present, and reset removes other stage folders and that key, then fails windows_profile_not_pristine (or windows_profile_residue_unproved when the probe cannot answer) if either survives. Before the mirror, reset stops test-user processes running from the resettable profile or WindowsApps. Processes in preserved directories stay live. Windows launches the Widgets packages (MicrosoftWindows.Client.WebExperience, Microsoft.WidgetsPlatformRuntime, and Microsoft.StartExperiencesApp) and the Microsoft Store package (Microsoft.WindowsStore) on its own. Every process in these packages stays running through reset because its state lives in preserved AppData/Local/Packages. Reset checks process ownership under the standard test user and names SSH discovery failures separately from desktop stop failures. The signed-in desktop session stops and reopens desktop apps, using the installed package's app identity or the per-user executable. Reset receipts name the stopped and relaunched apps and report relaunch failures without failing the restore. Copy failures from locked .codex files tell the operator to close Codex and retry. The per-user data store service's open database (AppData/Local/Comms) stays live like packaged-app containers, and copy failures name robocopy's failing files in the refusal. The mirror excludes Windows' System-marked profile compatibility junctions, which /MIR would otherwise purge. A native Windows host without control-plane access can read browser identity declarations from a UTF-8 file via --declarations-json @FILE, including the BOM written by Windows PowerShell 5.1. Machine-wide QA state comes from SYSTEM fixtures run through Azure run-command (yoke qa mission host-command --fixture NAME [--undo]: grant-admin, system-proxy-root-ca, applocker, task-scheduler-restricted, second-user), plus --elevated for the granted token and --second-user for the provisioned standard account Zoë Tester, whose password is never stored. An administrator token without --elevated refuses native_windows_test_user_required on its first command. Every native Windows reset runs every fixture undo before it restores, and a failed undo leaves the lab machine_needs_repair; the machine-baseline standard probe then fails probe_machine_drift for any leftover policy, proxy, CA, process, fixture file or group change, and a plain reset is its recovery, with a documented in-place OS-disk rebuild as the last resort.
